Wu Blockchain (@WuBlockchain): Vitalik Buterin: Without AI, Ethereum's Lean Roadmap Might Have to Wait Until 2040

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin @VitalikButerin   said in an October 9 interview with Balaji Srinivasan @balajis   at the Network State Conference 2026 that AI has become an important factor in advancing the Lean Ethereum roadmap. 

Buterin said that given the roadmap's current goals and level of ambition, without AI, the work might have taken until 2040 or even 2050 to complete. He added that AI is now contributing to a significant amount of research and coding, substantially accelerating progress on the roadmap.

COTI Foundation (@COTInetwork): Introducing COTI 2.0
Private Programmable Money

COTI shifts into its next phase, with a new website to match.
> http://coti.io

Same foundation. Bolder vision.

1. The Vision
The world's money will soon move the way information does, on open networks. But those networks are public, and nobody wants to run their finances in public.

COTI is now critically tasked with changing that. Its mission is to make private programmable money the global standard, so institutions, businesses, developers and individuals can hold, move and settle value on public blockchains, confidentially.

COTI exists to champion this cause.

2. The Foundation
Since 2017, COTI has built the privacy technology this next phase runs on. It was the first network to run garbled circuits in production, computing directly on encrypted data so inputs stay encrypted from submission to settlement.

Its institutional-grade technology has been developed across leading institutions:

1. European Central Bank
2. Bank of Israel
3. Input Output Global (IOG)

3. Privacy-on-Demand
Privacy-on-Demand serves as COTI's privacy layer for other blockchains. It allows applications to keep their users and assets on their existing chain, while COTI handles the private computation.

Avalanche was the first network to bring it to production. Since September 17, applications on Avalanche have been computing on confidential data, and users have been shielding AVAX and USDC through the Privacy Portal.

Expansion to further networks is a core part of the roadmap.

4. New Products
At the centre of COTI 2.0 are two new products, designed to keep transactions private when moving money between blockchains, and when spending it in day to day life.

1. Interphase - The flagship. It serves as the global privacy layer for moving assets between blockchains, and executing confidential, unlinked transfers across 30+ major networks.

2. COTI Global - A new central application, which allows COTI to be spent as a privacy payment rail for everything in day to day life.

5. What's Next
The new website and public roadmap are the first of several major upgrades coming this month.

Common Knowledge Base Association (CKBA) (@ckba_build): If Lightning is fundamentally a BTC payment network, how do you make other assets move through it?

There are several different approaches.

Taproot Assets, for example, keeps BTC liquidity at the center of the network.

When a user wants to send a Taproot Asset across Lightning, the asset is exchanged for BTC at the edge of the network. The payment then travels through ordinary BTC Lightning channels before being exchanged into the desired asset at the receiving edge.

That means most intermediate Lightning nodes can route the payment without ever needing to support or even recognize the Taproot Asset.

RGB pushes multi-asset support deeper into the route.

When a user wants to send an RGB asset across Lightning, that asset can travel through RGB-enabled channels from sender to receiver without being converted into BTC along the way.

The trade-off is liquidity: every channel on the chosen route must already have enough of that specific RGB asset on the forwarding side to pass the payment to the next hop. If even one channel lacks sufficient liquidity, that route cannot complete the payment.

Fiber starts from a third architecture.

Because CKB already supports user-defined assets at the base layer, Fiber doesn’t need to add a separate asset protocol on top of a BTC-only settlement layer. Supported CKB assets can be locked directly into Fiber channels and routed natively through the network.

These are three entirely different architectural approaches to the same problem, each with different trade-offs.

Check our latest article to learn more about how each solution works 👇

https://www.nervos.org/knowledge-base/how_payment_channel_networks_support_multiple_assets
